data.intent: Build a simple browser task list with English controls. I need to add tasks, mark individual tasks complete and delete tasks. Preserve the existing native ESM workspace. This first iteration needs no editing, bulk operations, filters or persistence.

domains.responsibility: Browser-rendered task list interface with English controls
In-memory task data and task operations (add, complete, delete) without persistence

features.responsibility: Allow the user to add a new task to the list via an English-labeled control
Allow the user to mark an individual task complete via an English-labeled control
Allow the user to delete an individual task via an English-labeled control

requirements.description: The user can enter task text and submit it; a new task appears in the task list with the entered text and is not marked complete.

acceptances.description: Entering text in the task input and submitting adds a task with that exact text to the visible list, not shown as complete.
Submitting with empty input does not add a task.

requirements.description: Each individual task provides a control to mark it complete; a completed task is visibly indicated.

acceptances.description: Activating the complete control on a task marks only that task as complete with a visible indication; other tasks remain unchanged.

requirements.description: Each individual task provides a control to delete it; deleting removes that task from the list.

acceptances.description: Activating the delete control on a task removes only that task from the visible list; other tasks remain unchanged.

requirements.description: All user-facing controls and labels are in English.

acceptances.description: Every visible control and label of the task list is in English.

constraints.description: The existing native ESM workspace must be preserved; the task list runs within it.
This first iteration excludes editing existing tasks, bulk operations, filters, and persistence; tasks exist only in memory for the session.

relations.description: Marking a task complete is only possible if a task has been added.
Deleting a task is only possible if a task has been added.

apps.name: Browser Task List
apps.description: Browser-rendered task list where the user can add tasks, mark individual tasks complete and delete them, with English controls.

modules.name: Task list UI
modules.description: Renders the task list UI with English labels (input field, Add button, Complete and Delete controls per task) and handles user interactions.

interfaces.name: User interaction events
interfaces.description: DOM event handlers that submit new task text and trigger complete/delete for a rendered task.

modules.name: Task state
modules.description: Holds the in-memory task array (text and completed flag) and performs add, complete-by-id and delete-by-id operations without persistence.

interfaces.name: Task operations
interfaces.description: Functions invoked by the UI module to add, complete and delete tasks and to return the current task list for re-rendering.

relations.description: The UI module calls the state module to apply task operations and re-renders the list from returned state.

scenarios.description: The user adds a task, then marks it complete and deletes it through English-labeled per-task controls.
scenarios.initial_state: Empty task list is displayed with an input and an Add button.

participants.name: User
participants.description: Browser user interacting with English-labeled controls.

steps.action: Enter task text and activate the Add control.
Request to add a task with the entered text.
Append the task (not completed) to the in-memory list and return the updated list.
Re-render the list showing the new task.
Activate the Complete control on that task.
Request to mark the task complete by identity.
Set the task's completed flag and return the updated list.
Activate the Delete control on that task.
Request to delete the task by identity.
Remove the task from the list and return the updated list.
Re-render the list without the deleted task.

outcomes.description: The list shows the new task with an English Complete and Delete control.
The task is marked complete and visibly indicated; other tasks unchanged.
The task is removed from the in-memory list and no longer rendered.

concepts.name: Task
concepts.definition: A task is an entry holding user-entered text and a completed flag, identified by a unique id for the current session.

rules.description: A task must have non-empty text; empty submissions do not create a task.
Complete and delete operations target exactly one task by its unique id.

decisions.name: Native ESM, no build step
decisions.decision: Keep the app as plain native ESM JavaScript modules (src/main.mjs) rendered into index.html, with no frameworks or build step.
decisions.reason: Preserves the existing workspace and avoids tooling for a small single-page UI.

decisions.name: In-memory session-only state
decisions.decision: Store tasks only in an in-memory array; a page reload clears the list, and no editing, bulk operations or filters are provided in this iteration.
decisions.reason: The confirmed first iteration explicitly excludes persistence and the listed operations.

risks.name: No persistence: tasks lost on reload
risks.description: Task data lives only in memory, so all tasks are lost when the page is reloaded or closed.
risks.impact: Users may lose their task list unexpectedly; acceptable for the confirmed first iteration.
risks.mitigation: Keep the state module isolated behind its operations interface so persistence can be added later without touching the UI.

diagrams.name: Task list overview
diagrams.description: High-level view of the browser task list app and its modules.

changes.description: In-memory task state module with addTask/completeTask/deleteTask/getTasks operations, unique ids, snapshot returns, and a test-only reset (OMOD-tasklist-state).

Browser task list UI module that mounts a text input, an English 'Add' button, and a list of tasks each with English 'Complete'/'Delete' controls; re-renders after every state operation (OMOD-tasklist-ui).
Native ESM browser entry now mounts the task list UI into the existing #app shell, preserving the native ESM workspace as required.
Node built-in tests for the state module covering add (with and without text, whitespace), complete-only-this-task, delete-only-this-task, no-op on unknown ids, and snapshot immutability.

Node built-in UI tests using a minimal DOM mock: mount renders English 'Add' input/button, per-task English 'Complete'/'Delete' controls, no add on empty/whitespace, complete marks only that task with visible strikethrough, delete removes only that task, Enter-key submit, and input clears after add.
